test_text: Frau Winkler kommt morgen nicht zur Arbeit, null sie Magenschmerzen hat.
tip: Subordinating conjunction for giving a reason (verb 'hat' is at the end).
meaning: Ms. Winkler is not coming to work tomorrow because she has a stomach ache.
grammar_tip: Use 'weil' when the conjugated verb stands at the very end of the clause.

test_text: Mein Hausarzt hat heute keine Sprechstunde, null muss ich bis morgen warten.
tip: Conjunctive adverb for expressing a consequence (verb 'muss' follows immediately).
meaning: My family doctor has no consultation hours today, so I have to wait until tomorrow.
grammar_tip: Use 'deshalb' when the conjugated verb immediately follows in position 2.

test_text: Er will mir nichts sagen, weil meine Krankheit so schlimm null.
tip: Verb goes to the end of a 'weil' clause.
meaning: He just doesn't want to tell me anything because my illness is so serious.
grammar_tip: In a subordinate clause with 'weil', the conjugated verb ('ist') goes to the very end.

test_text: Die Ärzte sagen nie die Wahrheit. Deshalb null ich gar nicht mehr hin.
tip: Verb in position 2 after 'Deshalb'.
meaning: The doctors never tell the truth. That's why I don't go there anymore at all.
grammar_tip: After 'Deshalb' in position 1, the conjugated verb ('gehe') stands in position 2 before the subject.

test_text: Du hast Probleme, null du zu viel auf deinen Körper hörst.
tip: Conjunction introducing a subordinate clause (verb 'hörst' at the end).
meaning: You have problems because you listen to your body too much.
grammar_tip: 'weil' introduces a Nebensatz with the conjugated verb at the end.

test_text: Du hörst zu viel auf deinen Körper. null hast du Probleme.
tip: Connector meaning 'therefore / that's why' followed by verb in position 2.
meaning: You listen to your body too much. That's why you have problems.
grammar_tip: 'Deshalb' connects a reason to a consequence and triggers subject-verb inversion ('hast du').

test_text: Eine Frau hat den Krankenwagen gerufen, weil meine Hand verletzt null.
tip: Past tense of 'sein' at the end of a 'weil' clause.
meaning: A woman called the ambulance because my hand was injured.
grammar_tip: Subordinate clause with 'weil': conjugated verb ('war') goes to the end.

test_text: Ich kann heute nicht zur Arbeit kommen, weil ich Fieber null.
tip: Conjugated verb 'haben' at the end of the 'weil' clause.
meaning: I cannot come to work today because I have a fever.
grammar_tip: In a 'weil' clause, 'ich habe' moves the verb 'habe' to the end.

test_text: Ich habe Fieber. Deshalb null ich heute nicht zur Arbeit kommen.
tip: Modal verb in position 2 after 'Deshalb'.
meaning: I have a fever. Therefore I cannot come to work today.
grammar_tip: After 'Deshalb', the conjugated modal verb ('kann') stands in position 2, and the infinitive ('kommen') goes to the end.

test_text: Gestern hatte ich einen null mit dem Fahrrad. (accident)
tip: Masculine noun in the accusative case.
meaning: Yesterday I had an accident with my bicycle.
grammar_tip: der Unfall → einen Unfall (accusative masculine).

test_text: Eine Frau hat sofort den null gerufen. (ambulance)
tip: Masculine compound noun in the accusative case.
meaning: A woman immediately called the ambulance.
grammar_tip: der Krankenwagen → den Krankenwagen (accusative masculine).

test_text: Meine Hand hat stark null. (bled)
tip: Partizip II of regular verb 'bluten'.
meaning: My hand bled heavily.
grammar_tip: Perfekt: hat + geblutet (bluten → geblutet).

test_text: Der Notarzt hat gemeint, dass ich ins null muss. (hospital)
tip: Neuter noun after 'ins' (in das).
meaning: The emergency doctor said that I have to go to the hospital.
grammar_tip: das Krankenhaus → in das (ins) Krankenhaus (accusative of direction).

test_text: In der null hat man meine Hand untersucht. (emergency room)
tip: Feminine noun in the dative case (location: Wo?).
meaning: In the emergency room they examined my hand.
grammar_tip: die Notaufnahme → in der Notaufnahme (dative feminine).

test_text: Man hat meine Hand im Krankenhaus null. (examined)
tip: Partizip II of inseparable verb 'untersuchen'.
meaning: They examined my hand at the hospital.
grammar_tip: Verbs with the inseparable prefix 'unter-' do not take 'ge-' in the Perfekt: untersucht.

test_text: Ich habe in der Klinik einen null bekommen. (bandage)
tip: Masculine noun in the accusative case.
meaning: I got a bandage at the clinic.
grammar_tip: der Verband → einen Verband (accusative masculine).

test_text: Die null hat nur fünf Minuten gedauert. (examination)
tip: Feminine noun ending in -ung as the subject.
meaning: The examination only lasted five minutes.
grammar_tip: die Untersuchung (nominative feminine).

test_text: Ich war heute bei meinem Hausarzt in der null. (consultation hour)
tip: Feminine noun in the dative case after 'in'.
meaning: I was at my family doctor's consultation hour today.
grammar_tip: die Sprechstunde → in der Sprechstunde (dative feminine).

test_text: Ich habe große Angst null Herzkrankheiten. (of)
tip: Fixed preposition with 'Angst haben'.
meaning: I am very afraid of heart diseases.
grammar_tip: Expression: Angst haben vor + dative.

test_text: Er hat Angst vor null Zahnarzt. (the)
tip: 'Angst haben vor' requires the dative case.
meaning: He is afraid of the dentist.
grammar_tip: vor + dative masculine (der Zahnarzt → dem Zahnarzt).
